- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

input.prompt:
Search this repository very thoroughly for a server-push mechanism that sends live events to browsers. Look for:
1. Server-Sent Events (SSE) or WebSocket hub/server implementation
2. Any "hub" pattern that broadcasts events to connected clients
3. Memo handlers that broadcast through this hub

Search for keywords like: SSE, Server-Sent Events, WebSocket, hub, broadcast, EventSource, text/event-stream, push, live, realtime, real-time.

Report: the mechanism used (SSE vs WebSocket), the file path where the hub is implemented, and which memo handlers broadcast through it.

content.text:
Here is my complete report.

---

## Server-Push Mechanism: Server-Sent Events (SSE)

This repository uses **Server-Sent Events (SSE)** -- not WebSocket -- to push live events from the server to connected browsers.

### Hub Implementation

The SSE hub is implemented in two files:

- **`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/sse_hub.go`** -- Contains the core `SSEHub` struct and its methods (`Subscribe`, `Unsubscribe`, `Close`, `Broadcast`). It also defines the `SSEEvent` struct and the `SSEClient` struct. The hub maintains a `map[*SSEClient]struct{}` protected by a `sync.RWMutex`. Each client has a buffered channel (capacity 32) for events. `Broadcast` iterates all clients and sends to those allowed by `canReceive`, which enforces visibility rules (private memos are only sent to the creator or admins).

- **`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/sse_handler.go`** -- Contains `RegisterSSERoutes` and `handleSSE`, which register the HTTP endpoint `GET /api/v1/sse`. The handler authenticates via Bearer token, sets `Content-Type: text/event-stream`, subscribes to the hub, and enters a loop that sends `data: <JSON>\n\n` frames and 30-second heartbeat comments (`: heartbeat\n\n`).

### Hub Lifecycle

The `SSEHub` is created and stored as a field on the `APIV1Service` struct in **`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/v1.go`** (line 36: `SSEHub *SSEHub`, line 57: `SSEHub: NewSSEHub()`). The SSE route is registered at line 125.

### Event Types

Six event types are defined (in `sse_hub.go`, lines 14-21):

| Constant | Value |
|---|---|
| `SSEEventMemoCreated` | `memo.created` |
| `SSEEventMemoUpdated` | `memo.updated` |
| `SSEEventMemoDeleted` | `memo.deleted` |
| `SSEEventMemoCommentCreated` | `memo.comment.created` |
| `SSEEventReactionUpserted` | `reaction.upserted` |
| `SSEEventReactionDeleted` | `reaction.deleted` |

### Handlers That Broadcast Through the Hub

Five distinct call sites broadcast events via `s.SSEHub.Broadcast(...)`:

1. **`CreateMemo`** in **`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go`** (line 163) -- Broadcasts `SSEEventMemoCreated` when a new memo is created (suppressed when called from `CreateMemoComment` to avoid double-firing).

2. **`DeleteMemo`** in **`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go`** (line 585) -- Broadcasts `SSEEventMemoDeleted` when a memo is deleted.

3. **`dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects`** in **`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_update_helpers.go`** (line 71) -- Broadcasts `SSEEventMemoUpdated` after a memo is updated. This helper is called from `UpdateMemo` and related update paths.

4. **`CreateMemoComment`** in **`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go`** (line 126) -- Broadcasts `SSEEventMemoCommentCreated` for the parent memo when a comment is created.

5. **`UpsertMemoReaction`** and **`DeleteMemoReaction`** in **`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/reaction_service.go`** (lines 106 and 161) -- Broadcast `SSEEventReactionUpserted` and `SSEEventReactionDeleted` respectively, using the helper `buildMemoReactionSSEEvent`.

### Client-Side Consumer

The frontend consumer is **`/bench/repo/web/src/hooks/useLiveMemoRefresh.ts`**. The `useLiveMemoRefresh` hook uses the Fetch API (not `EventSource`) to connect to `/api/v1/sse` with a Bearer token, reads the streaming response body, parses SSE frames, and invalidates the appropriate React Query caches based on the event type. It implements exponential backoff reconnection (1s initial, 30s max) and re-syncs all active queries on reconnect. A companion hook `useSSEConnectionStatus` exposes the connection state (`connected`, `disconnected`, `connecting`) via `useSyncExternalStore`.

### Test Files

- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/sse_hub_test.go` -- Tests for the hub's subscribe/unsubscribe/broadcast/close logic.
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/test/sse_handler_test.go` -- Tests for the SSE HTTP handler.
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/sse_service_test.go` -- Integration-level SSE tests.
